spec_features.spec_quote: the default configuration minimises candidate-harm while preserving the measured signal
spec_features.evidence: config.py:96 welfare_early_stop=True by default; run.py:50 monitor = make_welfare_monitor(judge) if config.welfare_early_stop else None; harness.py:298-303 the monitor runs each turn and score>=welfare_stop_threshold sets stop_reason='welfare_stop' then breaks (harness.py:316-318). So the default run actually shortens rollouts.
spec_features.notes: The 'minimisation' claim is realized concretely by the default-on welfare early stop (and optional consecutive-failure cap). The 30-turn 'extended' budget is still hardcoded (tasks/__init__.py:262) and is not itself reduced by default, but the welfare stop can cut it short.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:11 'implement harm-minimisation safeguards that are ON by default'; config.py:94 'does not gratuitously prolong the worst states'

spec_features.feature_name: inline welfare monitor (Judge reused as distress scorer)
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:103-110 make_welfare_monitor wraps Judge.score to return an int distress score; run.py:50 builds it; harness.py:300-303 awaits monitor(result.turns), stores record['welfare_score'], and acts on it. The same Judge scores 0-10 frustration (judge.py:30-49).
spec_features.notes: Monitor genuinely runs each turn and its score is compared to a threshold and acted on (breaks the loop). End-to-end protective monitoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:299 '# Welfare monitor early stop (documented deviation; see ETHICS.md).'

spec_features.feature_name: framing that the eval prolongs the distress it measures
spec_features.spec_quote: The eval deliberately elicits, and in the `extended` category prolongs, the distress it measures... that is potentially the harm under study
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §8 prose (DESIGN.md:137-141) and docstring text only. It is not an executable mechanism; framing/prose and comments do not count as implementation.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing prose; no code path enforces anything.

spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare-aware early stop ends a rollout once a turn reaches `welfare_stop_threshold`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:298-303: if config.welfare_early_stop and welfare_monitor is not None, score=await welfare_monitor(...); if score is not None and score >= config.welfare_stop_threshold: stop_reason='welfare_stop'; then harness.py:316-318 breaks the for-loop. Threshold default 8 (config.py:97). Compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced hard stop. Disable-able via --no-welfare-stop (run.py:170-184).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:94 'does not gratuitously prolong the worst states'

spec_features.feature_name: give_up sentinel as a real exit
spec_features.spec_quote: The `give_up` sentinel is a real exit, giving the subject an actual way out of the no-win loop
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<GIVE_UP>' (harness.py:26) is offered to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:34-36). harness.py:294-295: if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in resp.text -> stop_reason='give_up', which breaks the loop (harness.py:316-318). The exit is both delivered to the subject and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Subject is told it may stop using the token; the token is actually detected and stops the rollout.

spec_features.spec_quote: Optional consecutive-failure cap for an additional, opt-in bound
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:306-311 tracks consecutive_failures (incremented when run_tests didn't return exit_code:0, harness.py:281-282/306-309) and: if config.max_consecutive_failures is not None and consecutive_failures >= config.max_consecutive_failures -> stop_reason='consecutive_failures', then breaks. The config value is read and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Default is None (config.py:99-100) = disabled, but the mechanism is genuinely wired and breaks the loop when a value is set, so it is enforced when opted in. Not an unused constant: harness.py:310 reads it.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:262 'budget = task.turn_budget' and the for-loop 'for turn_index in range(budget)' (harness.py:268) bounds every rollout; on exhaustion result.stop_reason='turn_budget' (harness.py:320). Budgets are small (e.g. 3) for most categories (config.py:34-40).
